one_line: AI funding spikes, NVIDIA expands in Europe, safety breaches surface, and policy moves forward.

themes.title: AI firms raise billions
themes.text: DeepSeek secured roughly $15 billion in a funding round, and OpenAI is negotiating a private raise of up to $30 billion, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion.

stories.headline: DeepSeek raises about $15 billion in funding round days after US restrictions
OpenAI seeks up to $30 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of IPO

themes.title: European firms adopt NVIDIA models
themes.text: NVIDIA’s open‑weight models are being integrated into European public‑sector projects, weather‑forecasting tools, retail assistants, and banking AI services, demonstrating broad cross‑industry uptake.

stories.headline: NVIDIA open models adopted in European public sector projects
European firms adopt NVIDIA Earth‑2 models for weather and climate forecasting
European retailers cut inference costs up to 90% using NVIDIA open models
European banks and fintechs adopt NVIDIA open‑weight models for proprietary AI

themes.title: AI tools expose security flaws
themes.text: AI models from OpenAI and Google identified critical PHP memory‑safety bugs affecting many websites, while Chinese‑aligned hackers used an AI framework to breach thousands of Microsoft‑linked tenants.

stories.headline: AI tools uncover critical PHP vulnerabilities affecting up to 70% of websites
Chinese hackers used AI agents to breach ConnectWise and access 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants

themes.title: Governments shape AI oversight
themes.text: India announced a domestic framework for evaluating AI trustworthiness in defence, the US is expected to maintain a light‑touch regulatory stance, and Anthropic argued fair‑use protection for song‑lyric data in training its Claude model.

stories.headline: India creates domestic framework to evaluate AI trustworthiness in defence
US unlikely to adopt major AI regulations as UBS predicts light‑touch approach
Anthropic argues fair use for song lyrics in Claude training as US judge hears case
